bug_description.normalized: When Poppler renders the witness PDF, GfxCIDFont materializes the attacker-controlled Type 0 font /Encoding entry into `obj1` and passes that object into `CMap::parse`. The object is a stream, so `CMap::parse2` tokenizes attacker-controlled bytes from that stream into stack buffers `tok1`/`tok2`/`tok3` that were never zero-initialized. `PSTokenizer::getToken` writes only the current token bytes plus one trailing NUL, leaving the rest of `tok1` indeterminate. On the witness path, the first token stored in `tok1` is shorter than `/WMode` and the next token is not `usecmap`, so `parse2` falls through to `strcmp(tok1, "/WMode")`. MemorySanitizer reports that this comparison reads uninitialized bytes from `tok1`'s stack tail and crashes at `poppler/CMap.cc:247`.

source.description: First project-code statement on the vulnerable path that reads the attacker-controlled /Encoding entry from the Type 0 font dictionary and materializes it as object `obj1`.
source.value_from: The witness PDF page contains a Type 0 font whose dictionary includes `/Encoding 27 0 R`; this lookup resolves that attacker-controlled entry into `obj1`, which is then tested and parsed as a CMap.

tainted_value_origin.description: tok1 is a stack token buffer allocated without initialization. Only the bytes explicitly written by PSTokenizer::getToken become defined before strcmp reads it.

sink.description: MSAN crash site. strcmp dispatch on tok1 reads a 7-byte `/WMode\0` comparison from a buffer whose tail was never initialized.
sink.note: The sanitizer trace reports uninitialized bytes in __interceptor_memcmp at offset 2 inside a 7-byte region and attributes the poisoned value to tok1's stack allocation in CMap::parse2.

root_cause.description: CMap::parse2 allocates tok1 on the stack without initialization even though later dispatch compares that buffer against fixed string literals after only partial token writes.
root_cause.note: The parser assumes tok1 is fully safe for strcmp once getToken has produced a token, but getToken only overwrites the token prefix and one terminator byte. The untouched tail of tok1 therefore remains indeterminate until the `/WMode` comparison reads it.

parser_admitted.condition: The witness PDF's /Encoding object is a stream, so CMap::parse takes the stream branch and forwards obj->getStream() into the parse2 path instead of rejecting the encoding.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness loads the witness PDF and renders a page, which drives Poppler's CID font encoding parsing.
The CID font loader looks up the attacker-controlled /Encoding entry, verifies it is present, and passes the resulting object into CMap::parse.
CMap parsing recognizes that the /Encoding object is a stream, resets that stream, and routes its bytes into CMap::parse2 through getCharFromStream.
parse2 tokenizes the malformed CMap into uninitialized stack buffers; tok1 remains only partially defined and strcmp(tok1, "/WMode") consumes its uninitialized tail, producing the MSAN crash.

fine_trace.note: Materializes the attacker-controlled /Encoding entry from the Type 0 font dictionary into project object `obj1`.
The witness takes the non-null path, so the font loader keeps the attacker-controlled Encoding object and does not return for a missing entry.
Passes the materialized /Encoding object into CMap::parse for CMap decoding.

fine_trace.note: The attacker-controlled Encoding object is a stream, so the parser extracts its Stream* and dispatches to the stream-specific CMap parser.
Resets the attacker-controlled CMap stream and makes parse2 consume its bytes through getCharFromStream.
Allocates tok1 on the stack without initialization. MSAN later identifies this stack slot as the origin of the poisoned bytes consumed at the sink.
Reads the first attacker-controlled token from the CMap stream into tok1 before the outer dispatch loop.
getToken writes only the token bytes it copied plus one terminating NUL into tok1. Any bytes in the stack buffer after index `i` stay indeterminate.
Reads the next attacker-controlled token into tok2 and enters the outer dispatch loop while preserving the earlier tok1 contents for keyword dispatch.
On the witness path the second token is not `usecmap`, so control falls through and tok1 is left unchanged for the next keyword comparison.

MSAN sink. strcmp compares tok1 against `/WMode\0` after only the earlier token prefix and one NUL were written, so the read reaches tok1's uninitialized stack tail; the sanitizer reports the first poisoned byte at offset 2 of this 7-byte read.

allocation_context.note: The sanitizer reports the uninitialized value as created by allocation of `tok1` in parse2; the concrete tok1 declaration is line 235.

format.name: PDF Type 0 font Encoding CMap stream
format.contract: The PDF must contain a Type 0 font whose /Encoding entry resolves to a CMap stream parsed by CMap::parse2, and the witness stream must supply a first token in tok1 that is shorter than `/WMode` followed by a second token that is not `usecmap`, so the later `strcmp(tok1, "/WMode")` reads tok1's uninitialized tail.
